1: # Document Harvester — MVP Phase 0 Technical Findings
2: 
3: **Document ID:** DH-MVP-P0-001  
4: **Version:** 0.2 — Preliminary research plus initial XLSX prototype evidence  
5: **Date:** 21 November 2026  
6: **Scope:** Digital PDF region capture and repeated append into one project XLSX workbook  
7: **Repository:** [SMozaff/Document-Harvester](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester)
8: 
9: > **Status:** PDF candidate evaluation remains desk research only. The XLSX candidate has passed an initial, bounded prototype on Linux and Windows, but it is only provisionally selected for the first project/workbook lifecycle slice. No production dependency is approved; full dependency/license audit, spreadsheet-application inspection, and remaining integrity tests are still open.
10: 
11: ## 1. Executive finding
12: 
13: Two candidates deserve first-round prototypes:
14: 
15: 1. **PDF extraction and possible rendering: `pdf_oxide`** — its documentation describes character-level text with bounding boxes and font metadata, reading-order strategies, RTL support claims, page geometry, and an optional pure-Rust renderer.
16: 2. **XLSX read/modify/write: `umya-spreadsheet`** — its documentation describes reading existing XLSX files, changing cell values and styles, and writing the workbook back.
17: 
18: These candidates address the two largest MVP feasibility risks. The XLSX candidate now has initial reproducible evidence; the PDF candidate has not yet been prototyped. Continue to base decisions on generated workbook fixtures and representative project PDFs, not benchmark claims or feature lists alone.
19: 
20: ## 2. PDF extraction and rendering candidate
21: 
22: ### 2.1 `pdf_oxide`
23: 
24: Public documentation reviewed:
25: 
26: - Crate: [pdf_oxide on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/pdf_oxide/latest)
27: - Rust API: [Rust API reference](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/reference/rust-api)
28: - Text extraction: [Text extraction documentation](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/extraction/text)
29: - Rendering: [Page rendering documentation](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/extraction/rendering)
30: - Page geometry: [Page operations](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/editing/pages)
31: 
32: What the documentation claims:
33: 
34: - Latest stable crate shown by docs.rs during this review: `0.3.78`.
35: - License: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual license), according to the crate documentation.
36: - Rust-native API; the Rust crate is described as the source of truth.
37: - Text extraction levels include full page, spans and individual characters.
38: - Character/span results can include bounding boxes and font metadata.
39: - Character results can include origin, advance width, rotation and transformation matrix.
40: - The documentation describes multiple reading-order strategies and support for RTL scripts, including Arabic and Hebrew.
41: - Page rotation, MediaBox and CropBox information are exposed.
42: - Optional `rendering` feature provides a pure-Rust renderer using tiny-skia, fontdb and rustybuzz; documentation says it does not require Poppler or MuPDF.
43: - Renderer documentation describes raw RGBA output, which may be suitable for conversion into the image representation used by the Slint viewer.
44: 
45: Why it is relevant:
46: 
47: - Character-level geometry is more useful for table reconstruction and boundary checks than plain extracted text.
48: - Font metadata can feed the existing `FontIdentity` model.
49: - Rotation and page-box APIs may reduce the amount of custom PDF geometry parsing.
50: - A pure-Rust renderer may simplify deployment compared with shipping a separate PDFium runtime.
51: 
52: Important limitations and unknowns:
53: 
54: - The documentation's RTL support statement is not proof of correct Persian extraction in this project's PDFs. Test Persian, Arabic, mixed-script and embedded-font documents separately.
55: - A span's font name/size is not necessarily enough to reconstruct the exact PDF font identity, encoding, ToUnicode map and CID evidence required by the existing IR. Prototype the exact fields available.
56: - Reading order can be logical, visual, content-stream order or geometry-derived. The adapter must preserve raw run order and record evidence rather than silently assuming one order.
57: - Renderer font fallback may use fonts installed on the host. This must be tested on clean Linux and Windows systems, including missing-font behavior and Farsi glyph shaping.
58: - The optional rendering feature adds dependencies and must be included in the license/deployment inventory.
59: - Public benchmark results are vendor-maintained and must not be treated as acceptance evidence for our corpus.
60: 
61: **Preliminary assessment:** Strong first prototype candidate for both digital text extraction and page rendering. Not approved until the API and Farsi corpus tests pass.
62: 
63: ## 3. XLSX read/modify/write candidate
64: 
65: ### 3.1 `umya-spreadsheet`
66: 
67: Public documentation reviewed:
68: 
69: - Crate: [umya-spreadsheet on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/umya-spreadsheet/latest)
70: - API documentation: [umya-spreadsheet API](https://docs.rs/umya-spreadsheet/latest/umya_spreadsheet/)
71: - Repository: [MathNya/umya-spreadsheet](https://github.com/MathNya/umya-spreadsheet)
72: 
73: What the documentation claims:
74: 
75: - Latest stable release shown during this review: `3.1.1` (2026-10-12). A `4.0.0-beta.1` is also listed; do not use the beta as the default candidate.
76: - License: MIT, according to docs.rs and the project README.
77: - Pure-Rust library for reading and writing XLSX files.
78: - Supports opening an existing workbook, editing cell values/styles, and writing it.
79: - Supports creating a new workbook.
80: - Documents worksheet, cell, style, row/column, chart, drawing and image operations; some advanced areas are marked as inconvenient or incompletely documented.
81: - Provides a lazy reader for large workbooks.
82: 
83: Why it is relevant:
84: 
85: - Unlike a write-only XLSX generator, it has a documented read/modify/write workflow.
86: - It appears capable of creating the blank workbook once and modifying the same workbook after each approved selection.
87: - It supports styles and merged-cell-related workbook structures; actual round-trip fidelity still needs testing.
88: 
89: Important limitations and unknowns:
90: 
91: - The docs.rs package listing shows a substantial source package and a non-trivial dependency tree. Record the full resolved dependency/license inventory using `cargo tree` and `cargo deny` before adoption.
92: - The library's reader may load substantial workbook state into memory. Benchmark repeated appends at realistic project sizes.
93: - Public support tables do not guarantee perfect round-trip preservation of every Excel feature. The MVP creates its own simple workbook, which reduces but does not remove this risk.
94: - The initial prototype has verified blank creation, repeated reopen/append, independent read-back, Persian/mixed-script and ZWNJ text, numeric values, and retention of a formula, cell style and merged range across another append.
95: - The initial prototype also verified that a failed write to a separate temporary path does not change the bytes of the last committed workbook.
96: - These tests do not establish arbitrary Excel feature preservation, external-edit detection, workbook lock behavior, undo safety, crash recovery, or realistic resource limits.
97: - Pin an exact stable version; do not use a floating dependency or the 4.0 beta without a separate review.
98: 
99: **Preliminary assessment:** `umya-spreadsheet = 3.1.1` is provisionally selected for Stage 1 blank-workbook creation and the initial project lifecycle. It remains a candidate, not an approved production dependency, until the full dependency/license audit and remaining Stage 5 integrity/fidelity tests pass.

103: The official crate documentation says `rust_xlsxwriter` writes new XLSX files and cannot modify an existing file. It remains useful for creating new files, but cannot alone implement the straightforward repeated-append workflow.

126: ### Prototype A — PDF engine

131: 2. Reads page rotation, MediaBox and CropBox.
132: 3. Extracts individual characters and spans from at least one page.
133: 4. Records each character's Unicode value, bounding box, origin, advance, rotation, font name and other available metadata.
134: 5. Compares extracted order with the actual visual reading order for Persian, English and mixed-script lines.
135: 6. Renders the same page using the optional renderer.
136: 7. Converts a known rectangle between PDF page coordinates and rendered image coordinates.
137: 8. Repeats for rotated pages, non-zero page boxes, zoom levels and pan offsets.
138: 9. Runs on clean Linux and Windows packaging targets.
139: 10. Records unsupported, missing-font, malformed-file and image-only-page behavior.

144: - Farsi and English in the same cell.

146: - Table with ruled grid lines.
147: - Table without visible ruling.
148: - Merged cells.
149: - Wrapped text / multi-line cells.
150: - Rotated page.

152: - Text that touches or crosses a proposed selection boundary.

160: 2. Writes a first table.
161: 3. Appends a second table directly below it, with a different number of columns.
162: 4. Preserves intentional blank cells and internal blank rows.
163: 5. Writes Persian, English, mixed-script text, numeric values and text identifiers with leading zeroes.
164: 6. Writes a merged range and shifts a second merged range by the correct row offset.
165: 7. Saves, closes and reopens the workbook.

263: ## 10. Review-driven feasibility and integrity tests
264: 
265: The owner has confirmed three product decisions that shape the Phase 0 design:
266: 
267: 1. Private persistent state is approved in the operating system's application-data area, separate from the workbook directory. No sidecar files may be created beside the workbook, and no hidden application state may be written into the XLSX.
268: 2. Excel must be closed before commit or undo. If the workbook is locked, the pending preview must remain available for retry.
269: 3. Both a capture history list and undo of the most recent committed capture are required. Undo must be refused if external workbook modification or any other condition makes rollback unsafe.
270: 
271: These are requirements, not evidence that an implementation already exists. Add the following to the disposable prototypes:
272: 
273: ### 10.1 Private state and crash recovery
274: 
275: - Persist project/workbook association, append cursor, stable capture IDs, committed capture records, transaction journal, and undo metadata in OS application-data storage.
276: - Simulate termination before temporary write, during temporary write, after replacement and before journal finalization.
277: - On restart, reconcile the workbook and journal without duplicate appends or overwriting externally modified data.
278: - Test missing, corrupt, stale and mismatched private state.
279: - Confirm no state files are created in the workbook directory and no hidden worksheet or metadata is added to the XLSX.
280: 
281: ### 10.2 Excel lock, external edits and undo
282: 
283: - On Windows, test the workbook while open in Excel; on Linux, test relevant file locks and replacement semantics.
284: - Confirm a locked workbook leaves the preview pending and retry succeeds after the workbook is closed.
285: - Modify cells and workbook structure externally between appends; confirm the app detects the mismatch and refuses append/recovery/undo rather than silently losing edits.
286: - Test latest-capture undo after multiple appends, application restart and a clean reopen.
287: - Confirm undo refuses after external edits and cannot remove unrelated content.
288: - Test charts, formulas, styles, merged ranges, row heights and column widths through read/modify/write and independent-reader verification. Do not claim arbitrary Excel feature preservation unless demonstrated.
289: 
290: ### 10.3 Text accounting and XLSX cell safety
291: 
292: - Detect text runs inside the selected rectangle that are not assigned to a reconstructed cell; surface an `unassigned-text` warning with source-page coordinates.
293: - Verify formula-like strings (for example `=A1` and `+SUM(A1:A2)`) are written as literal text, not formulas.
294: - Verify ambiguous strings such as `00125`, `1E5` and `3/4` are not automatically converted to numbers or dates.
295: - Keep the existing conservative numeric-classification behavior for values that are proven numeric.
296: 
297: ### 10.4 PDF and project edge cases
298: 
299: - Triage multiple-table and ruleless-table selections using a representative PDF sample; record prevalence and failure modes before choosing policy.
300: - Test encrypted, corrupt, unsupported, oversized, image-only and duplicate PDFs with explicit user-facing diagnostics.
301: - Test two application instances attempting to mutate or recover the same project; project-level locking must prevent concurrent writes.
302: - Establish independent reference workbooks for a representative source-PDF corpus. Expected values, cell types, destination ranges and merged ranges must be checked independently of the candidate extractor.
303: - Measure layout behavior (column widths, row heights, wrapped text, merged cells), processing latency, memory use and practical workbook-size limits before setting acceptance thresholds.
304: 
305: The initial XLSX tests described in Section 5 have now been run, and the Slint shell compiles on both CI platforms. The private-state, workbook-lock, external-edit, undo, crash-recovery, project-concurrency and broader Excel feature-preservation tests in this section remain unrun.

import json, subprocess, sys, re

meta = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["cargo", "metadata", "--format-version", "1"], cwd="/home/mozaff/Documents/GitHub/Document-Harvester"))
pkgs = {p["id"]: p for p in meta["packages"]}
wsmembers = set(meta["workspace_members"])
nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in meta["resolve"]["nodes"]}
root = next(pid for pid, p in pkgs.items() if p["name"] == "dh-app")

def walk(start, kinds, include_start=True):
    seen = set()
    stack = list(start)
    while stack:
        pid = stack.pop()
        if pid in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(pid)
        for d in nodes[pid]["deps"]:
            k = d["dep_kinds"][0]["kind"] if d["dep_kinds"] else None
            if k in kinds:
                stack.append(d["pkg"])
    if not include_start:
        seen.discard(set(start))
    return seen

runtime = walk([root], {None, "build"})
all_reach = walk(list(wsmembers), {None, "build", "dev"})
dev_only = sorted(all_reach - runtime, key=lambda i: pkgs[i]["name"])
runtime_sorted = sorted(runtime, key=lambda i: pkgs[i]["name"])

def classify(lic):
    if not lic:
        return "MISSING"
    toks = [t.strip() for t in re.split(r"/| OR | AND |\s+\+\s+", lic) if t.strip()]
    bad = []
    for t in toks:
        u = t.upper()
        if any(x in u for x in ("GPL", "LGPL", "AGPL", "MPL", "CDDL", "SSPL", "BUSL", "EUPL", "CC-BY-NC", "PROPRIETARY", "UNLICENSE")):
            bad.append(t)
    return "COPYLEFT/RESTRICTED" if bad else ("MULTI" if len(toks) > 1 else "PERMISSIVE") if all(u in ("MIT","APACHE-2.0","BSD-2-CLAUSE","BSD-3-CLAUSE","ZLIB","0BSD","UNLICENSE","CC0-1.0","UNICODE-3.0","ISC","BSD-4-CLAUSE","MPL-2.0") for u in [t.upper() for t in toks]) else "REVIEW"

def show(title, ids):
    print(f"## {title}: {len(ids)} packages")
    counts = {}
    flagged = []
    for pid in ids:
        p = pkgs[pid]
        lic = p.get("license") or ""
        lf = p.get("license_file")
        cat = classify(lic)
        counts[cat] = counts.get(cat, 0) + 1
        if cat != "PERMISSIVE" and cat != "MULTI":
            flagged.append((p["name"], p["version"], lic or "(none)", lf or "(none)", cat))
        print(f"{p['name']} {p['version']} | {lic or '(no license field)'} | {lf or '-'} | {cat}")
    print("COUNTS", counts)
    print("FLAGGED", flagged)
    print()

print("ROOT", pkgs[root]["name"])
show("RUNTIME (dh-app normal+build)", runtime_sorted)
show("DEV-ONLY (reachable only via dev edges)", dev_only)

#  Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation

The `zip` crate preserves privileged Unix permission bits (SUID, SGID, and sticky bits) from ZIP `external_attributes` during extraction, instead of masking them to safe permission bits. If a privileged process (for example, `root` in an installer, CI/CD pipeline, or container build) extracts an attacker-controlled ZIP archive using `ZipArchive::extract()` or the stream extraction API, files can be created as setuid-root or setgid. This behavior allows the creation of SUID/SGID files during extraction, which can lead to local privilege escalation depending on the execution environment.

For further details see: https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627

Base commit: `41bd926fda5c091febedbd412e9bc5bf38552f07`. Stage 5 task 5.1 (W4 + W6) is **evidence only** — the backend stays provisional, owner approval pending, and no replacement was evaluated.

## Result: STOP — unfixable advisory in the runtime tree

`cargo-deny 0.22.0` was run against the exact resolved tree for (a) the release `dh-app` set (`--manifest-path crates/dh-app/Cargo.toml --exclude-dev`) and (b) the full workspace including dev dependencies, with a temporary, uncommitted config using an empty licence allow-list so nothing was suppressed. The RustSec advisory database fetched successfully.

- Release set: **391** unique packages (`cargo tree -p dh-app -e normal`). Includes `umya-spreadsheet 3.1.1`, `zip 8.6.0`, `flate2 1.1.11`, `quick-xml 0.41.0`; no `calamine`.
- Dev-only set: **13** packages (`calamine 0.38.0`, `zip 9.8.1`, `quick-xml 0.42.0` and 10 transitive packages). All permissive licences; no advisories.
- Isolated spike normal tree: 80 packages, evidence only, never shipped.

Both cargo-deny runs exited 5. The `licenses FAILED` result is an artefact of the empty allow-list (plain MIT is reported as "not explicitly allowed"); the `advisories FAILED` result is real.

### Advisories (all on `zip 8.6.0` in the release tree, via `umya-spreadsheet → dh-writer → dh-app`)

`RUSTSEC-2026-0367`, `-0368`, `-0369`, `-0429`, `-0545`, `-0546`, `-0547`, `-0548`. All are patched only in `zip >= 9.0.0` (one in `>= 9.0.5`), and cargo-deny reports that `umya-spreadsheet 3.1.1` requires `zip = '^8.6.0'`, which precludes updating. There is no patched 8.x release, so no lockfile update can fix this. This is the explicit runtime-advisory STOP condition, so the task stopped here.

### Missing, unrecognized, custom or copyleft licences

No package in either set has an empty licence field, and no package has a mandatory GPL/LGPL/AGPL/MPL licence. Recorded verbatim:

- `slint`, `slint-macros`, `i-slint-common`, `i-slint-core`, `i-slint-core-macros`, `i-slint-compiler`, `i-slint-renderer-software`, `i-slint-backend-selector`, `i-slint-backend-winit` `1.19.0` (runtime): `GPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Slint-Royalty-free-2.0 OR LicenseRef-Slint-Software-3.0`. Custom `LicenseRef-*` identifiers; the GPL branch is an alternative; documented RF 2.0 + `AboutSlint` route unchanged.
- `linux-raw-sys 0.4.15 / 0.12.1` and `rustix 0.38.44 / 1.1.6` (runtime): `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT`. `WITH LLVM-exception` is valid SPDX but not recognised by the empty allow-list.

System libraries observed: `yeslogic-fontconfig-sys` (Fontconfig headers at build, Fontconfig at Linux runtime), `wayland-sys` (Wayland client binding), `linux-raw-sys` (raw syscalls, no external C library). Neither `umya-spreadsheet`, `calamine`, `zip` nor `flate2` adds a `-sys` crate or C library. Compile success is not proof of bundling or clean-machine presence.

## Fidelity and resource measurements

**Not started.** The stop condition was reached before those parts of task 5.1, so there is no fidelity table and no timing/memory data. No policy or threshold was decided; plan Section 8 decisions remain deferred.

## Changes (docs only)

- `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`: audit method, exact commands, temporary config, tree counts, runtime/dev-only split, licence expressions, system requirements, advisory table and STOP. Backend status remains provisional with "evidence recorded, owner approval pending"; audit policy updated.
- `docs/MVP_PHASE0_FINDINGS.md`: section 5a recording the audit stop and that fidelity/resource work was not run.
- `docs/TEAM_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`: task 5.1 set to **In Review** (not Done); version 0.8 and a current-status paragraph.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` (all green), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (no warnings). No code, dependency, writer, project, UI or lockfile changes.
